Rule: Use snake_case inspection, unit, room and check refs. Provide condition for each check; use unrecorded when unknown. Photos are media refs, never URLs.
Rule: Use style "rooms" to record evidence and "report" for a read-only summary. Set finalisedAt only for a signed-off record with no unrecorded checks; previousRef is a different report.
Rule: To hide the previous report reference, set detail to "brief" and retain previousRef and the evidence. For brief alone, use exactly {"detail":"brief","density":null,"surface":null} for the variant fields. Null keeps the app settings; never fill unrequested defaults.
Rule: Opt checks into tenant review with tenantSignoff "pending". Use "signed" only for an already co-signed check. Put supplied tenant dispute text in disputeComment, separate from the inspector’s note.

RentRoll: - RentRoll: Reconcile monthly rent charges and receipts across units, including part payments and arrears. Pick: Reconcile rent charges and allocated or voided receipts by unit and period, or show a resident their own rent ledger. Not one sum (Amount), one client's payment (PaymentStatus), an invoice (Invoice), or personal bills (Bills).

Rule: Every receipt references a charge in this line; keep older charges when needed for arrears. Seed obligations and allocations only, not computed receipt totals, outstanding, arrears, credit or statuses.
Rule: Give each charge and each receipt its own snake_case reference. Charges and receipts use positive numbers, not currency text. Use style "outstanding" only to filter unpaid units.
Rule: If asked to shorten numbers, set figures to "short". Leave density null unless the person asks for tighter rows, even when figures is "short".
Rule: Use style "tenant" only for a resident’s own rent ledger. Supply their tenantLetRef and only charges from that let and receipts allocated to them. Write autopay only when its on/off status is supplied.

Rule: Use snake_case references. Every let must reference a unit in this line. Active lets for one unit must not overlap; the end date is exclusive, and cancelled lets do not count.
Rule: A stay requires an end date and per "night"; a tenancy uses "week" or "month". Supply askingRent and askingPer together, or omit both. Do not write occupancy or totals.
Rule: Do not copy unrequested photos, addresses or links from the example. A requested thumbnail sets only media to "thumb". Usual, regular or default spacing and surface mean null for density and surface, never explicit defaults.
Rule: For a Vacancies view (vacant and notice-given units), set style to "vacancies". Otherwise set style to "register". Always write every supplied unit and let, even in the Vacancies view: the view, not the Writer, filters their visibility.
Rule: For a tenancy described as on notice, write the given notice date in noticeGivenOn. Its end must be later than notice. Do not use a scheduled end alone as notice.

Viewings: - Viewings: Arrange property viewings and track each prospect’s confirmation and attendance. Pick: Property viewing appointments with a unit, prospect, confirmation, invitation or attendance outcome. Not a day's timed agenda (Timeline), free slots (Slots), or a booked service (Appointment).
RequestQueue: - RequestQueue: Find the next service request to work on by urgency and deadline. Pick: An operator's active and completed service tickets, grouped by lifecycle status and ordered by urgency and deadline. Not a short tappable badge list (List), arbitrary stages (Board), or one rental repair (Request).
RequestResolution: - RequestResolution: Verify a repair outcome, accept it or reopen the original request. Pick: Save a proposed repair outcome with evidence and verification checks, then let the requester accept it or reopen the same service ticket. Not a conversation or status updates (RequestThread), a success message (Success), a star rating (Scale), or contract terms (Agreement).
RequestThread: - RequestThread: Follow one request through staff updates, work events and replies. Pick: One service ticket's replies interleaved with typed status, assignment and work-order events, with staff-only or requester-visible audiences. Not an ordinary chat (Bubbles), read-only history (Timeline), general audit (ActivityLog), or post replies (Comments).
RequestTriage: - RequestTriage: Prioritise and route a report, or link it to an existing request. Pick: Triage one incoming service report: compare reported urgency with impact, set effective priority and route it or link a duplicate. Not a simple form dropdown (Field) or manager permission (Approval).
WorkOrder: - WorkOrder: Carry out a repair with required checks, time and parts used. Pick: One assigned execution record tied to a service request, with required checks, time and consumed parts. Not simple jobs to tick (Checklist), attendance (TimeClock), or a booked visit (Appointment).
Challenge: - Challenge: Join a shared goal and track the group’s and your own progress. Pick: A group challenge with a shared goal, deadline, group total, personal contribution and up to three leaders. Not a personal goal (Progress) or a full leaderboard (List).
Comments: - Comments: Read and respond to replies under a shared post. Pick: Public replies beneath a post, with author avatars, like and reply controls, and one level of indentation. Not a two-person private conversation (Bubbles) or a business review (Review).
EventCard: - EventCard: See a community event and say whether you’re going or interested. Pick: An event to join in a community, with its date block, attendees and Going or Interested controls. Not organising one's own gathering (events), a provider booking (Appointment), or a featured preview without RSVPs (Card).
Feed: - Feed: Browse recent posts shared by several people. Pick: Several community posts to scroll, with authors, short excerpts and reactions. Not one full post (Post), ordinary tappable rows (List), a private journal (Entries), or chat messages (Bubbles).
Invite: - Invite: Bring new members in with a code they can share or scan. Pick: Invite people to join an app or group using a copyable, shareable code and optional QR. Not sharing a post (Post) or listing existing members (People).
Poll: - Poll: Ask a group to vote and see how everyone voted. Pick: A shared question with voting options and group results. Not a choice for oneself (Choice), a quiz with right answers (Quiz), or coordinating a date via availability (FindDate).
Post: - Post: Read and react to one community post in full. Pick: One community post in full, with author, long text, optional photo carousel and like, comment and share controls. Not several posts (Feed), an article (Article), or one featured thing preview (Card).
Stories: - Stories: Tap through people’s short-lived updates and add one of your own. Pick: Short-lived stories from people, opened from seen or unseen avatar rings, with an optional add button first. Not a member roster (People) or a photo collection (Gallery).
Bracket: - Bracket: Follow knockout ties and see who advances to the next round. Pick: A knockout cup as paired teams per round, with winners advancing. Only use it for actual head-to-head ties; a top-scorers ranking is List, even in a cup. Not a league table (Standings) or a sequence of matches (Fixtures).
Fixtures: - Fixtures: See who we play next and how recent matches ended. Pick: A team’s fixture schedule and results: opponents, venues and home or away, or one next-match card with meet time and kit. Not dates alone (Calendar), live scoring (Scoreboard), an appointment (Appointment) or a community event (EventCard).
Lineup: - Lineup: See where the starters play and who is on the bench. Pick: Starters arranged in their playing lines on a pitch or grouped by position, with a separate substitutes bench. Not an ordinary list of people (People), player availability (Squad) or a staff rota (Roster).
MatchFeed: - MatchFeed: See each side's match incidents and record a new one. Pick: Home and away incidents within one match by minute: goals, cards, substitutions and notes. Not a one-sided history or daily plan (Timeline) or community posts (Feed).
Scoreboard: - Scoreboard: Follow the current score or keep score for both sides. Pick: The score and match clock for one contest between a home side and an away side. Not a practice result (Result), one adjustable count (Counter) or a standalone clock (Timer).
Squad: - Squad: See who can play and let the coach pick the side. Pick: Players' availability for one upcoming match: yes, maybe or no, an optional reason, and coach selection. Not an ordinary player directory (People), who plays where (Lineup), guest RSVPs (GuestList), or staff shifts (Roster).
Standings: - Standings: Compare teams in a league and see our place in the season. Pick: A league table with played, wins, draws, losses, goal difference, points and recent form. Not a ranking on one value (List) or a general records table (Table).
Approval: - Approval: Review staff requests and decide whether to approve or decline them. Pick: A manager decides on submitted staff requests such as time off, swaps and expenses. Not jobs to tick off (Checklist) or a client accepting a quote (Invoice).
Handover: - Handover: Read what the last shift passed on and mark each note as seen. Pick: Read shift-to-shift notes with author, time, optional flag and a mark-as-seen control. Not writing your own note (Composer), chatting (Bubbles), or a record change log (ActivityLog).
OpenShift: - OpenShift: Pick up an unassigned shift and see when it runs and what it pays. Pick: Claim one of several unassigned work shifts with a date, time range, role and optional pay. Not an assigned shift (Shift) or a list of jobs to tick off (Checklist).
Roster: - Roster: See who works each day this week and spot gaps in cover. Pick: A weekly grid comparing staff shift times across people and days. Not one person's daily schedule (Timeline), one shift (Shift), bookable hours (Availability), a sports lineup (Lineup), or class periods (Timetable).
Shift: - Shift: See one assigned shift and ask to swap it or offer it to someone else. Pick: One assigned staff shift with start and end times, coworkers and swap or offer actions. Not a record preview (Card), the whole rota (Roster), or a client's booking (Appointment).
TimeClock: - TimeClock: Clock in and out of a work shift and record breaks. Pick: Record work attendance with clock-in, clock-out and breaks for the current shift. Not a stopwatch or countdown for an activity (Timer), or approving a week's hours (Timesheet).
Timesheet: - Timesheet: Review and approve the hours each person worked during a week. Pick: Review each worker's actual hours for seven days and approve their weekly row. Not a chart of daily totals (Bars), a planned rota (Roster), or a generic table (Table).
BagTracker: - BagTracker: See where my checked bags were scanned and where to collect them. Pick: Track several checked bags by tag across airline scan checkpoints. Not guided steps (Steps), trip packing (PackingList), parcels (DeliveryTracker) or retail orders (OrderStatus).
CabinSeats: - CabinSeats: Choose or change a numbered seat on a flight or train. Pick: Pick or change a numbered seat on a flight or train using an aisle map, with optional upgrade fees. Not fare tier options (Choice), banquet tables (Seating), or cinema seats (SeatPicker).
Clocks: - Clocks: Compare local time in several places with the time back home. Pick: Current local clock times in two to four named time zones, with offsets from home. Not elapsed or remaining time (Timer) or scheduled events (Timeline).
Converter: - Converter: Convert between home and local currencies by entering either amount. Pick: Convert two editable amounts between home and destination currencies with a swap control. Not displaying one sum (Amount) or entering an expense (AmountPad).
FlightStatus: - FlightStatus: Track one booked flight's live status, airport details and progress. Pick: Live operational status, gate updates and progress for one specific flight. Not static facts (KeyValue), a boarding pass (Reservation) or airport-wide boards (Departures).
Itinerary: - Itinerary: See the whole trip day by day, including stops and travel between them. Pick: A whole trip grouped into foldable dated days with places, timed stops and travel legs. Not a single day's time order (Timeline), a path through places (Route), or a family week (Agenda).
PackingList: - PackingList: Pack by category or person, track quantities and see what remains. Pick: Items to put in luggage, grouped by category or traveller, with optional quantities and an overall packed share. Not everyday tasks (Checklist) or shopping for groceries (GroceryList).
Reservation: - Reservation: Keep a travel confirmation, reference and gate pass together. Pick: One travel or lodging confirmation, with a copyable reference, optional seat and optional scannable pass. Not simple label/value facts (KeyValue), booking a provider (Appointment), running an event (Ticket), or buying goods (OrderSummary).
TravelDocs: - TravelDocs: Keep travel documents together and see whether they expire near the trip. Pick: A travel document wallet with owners, masked numbers and expiry warnings. Not facts about one thing (KeyValue) or warranties for belongings (Warranties).
Weather: - Weather: See the forecast or typical weather for the place and dates of a trip. Pick: A place's local weather or trip forecast, including conditions and rain chance. Not personal figures (Stats) or a series showing a trend (Sparkline).
